newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SOCCER-MALAYSIA HOLD THAILAND TO 1-1 DRAW IN TIGER CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALAYSIA HOLD THAILAND TO 1-1 DRAW IN TIGER CUP.

text.p: Malaysia came into the Tiger Cup not expecting to achieve much but on Sunday they surprised themselves by holding highly-rated Thailand to a 1-1 draw in a match they finished with only 10 men.

The unlikely result for a team whose form had been indifferent and whose coach had declared he was deliberately blooding younger players left Malaysia well placed for one of the two group B berths for Friday's semifinals.
Malaysia are third in the group, two points behind Singapore and Thailand, and are likely to beat Brunei in their last group encounter.
Brunei beat the Philippines 1-0 on Sunday in a match between teams who had lost all their previous matches. The goal was scored by Irwan Mohammed in the 28th minute
Singapore and Thailand, leading the group with seven points each, meet on Tuesday. Neither side is confident of winning but both know defeat would most likely cost them a semifinal place.
A flamboyant Thai move set the game alight in the 28th minute, culminating in a great volleyed goal by 20-year-old Kiatasuk Senamuang from 30 metres.
Zainal Abidin Hassan equalised for Malaysia in the 57th minute, scoring with a free-kick which pierced the Thai defensive wall.
But Malaysia had to endure an uneasy final few minutes after defender Faisal Zainal was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 83rd minute.
Zainal, who received a booking in last week's Tiger Cup opener against Singapore, must wait until Monday to hear whether he will miss one or two matches.
